clue.text: Physician’s helper trains cats to do something initially unnatural

indicators.note: something unnatural is not in its normal state, so these letters leave their usual order
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as raw material
the opening letter of something

explanation.surface: A doctor's aide spends their time teaching cats to perform tricks no cat would do naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior hospital doctor working under a senior physician is literally that physician's helper.

clue.text: Marg as an alternative is one of these

definitions.text: Marg as an alternative is one of these

indicators.note: an alternative version of the letters is a different arrangement of them

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Margarine offered as a substitute for butter is one of a family of spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: rearranging MARG AS AN gives the answer, and that very rearrangement is one example of what the answer names. Marg is British shorthand for margarine.
explanation.definitionFit: Words formed by rearranging the letters of other words are called this, and the clue's own trick is one such rearrangement.

clue.text: Foolish grandma that is welcoming

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, meaning that is
nan is an informal word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A silly grandmother greeting her visitors at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane describes something silly or senseless, a straightforward synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Mishap’s found in Dallas, Rev Erikson upset

indicators.note: the letters are found in the run of words that follows, spanning the gaps between them
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the letters straddle dalLAS REV ERikson

explanation.surface: A news story about some misfortune befalling a clergyman named Erikson in Dallas.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the name of the very device used to clue it, a fitting touch in a puzzle themed on clue types.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a setback or change for the worse in someone's fortunes, so it serves as a mishap.

clue.text: ‘Solvable’, you said for a match

indicators.note: the words point to how something is pronounced, not how it is written

blocks.note: solvable means doable, which spoken quickly comes out like the answer

explanation.surface: A sports commentator calling a fixture winnable.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is an exact counterpart or duplicate of something, which is what a perfect match is.

clue.text: Old monarch’s family good, agreed to be employed when lacking English

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken away
letters put to work are reshaped for a new use, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: kin are your family
G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A historical monarch's relatives consented to be given jobs on condition that the English were absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one E of agreed goes, leaving five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar the Peaceful ruled England in the tenth century, so he is a monarch from long ago.

clue.text: Discovered orchid Dennis covered

indicators.note: something discovered has been found lurking within, here inside the next two words

blocks.note: the letters run across orcHID DENnis

explanation.surface: A gardener named Dennis found an orchid that had been kept under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like the definition, but it means the opposite of the answer; it is the signal, and 'covered' at the end defines. The answer also names the clue type.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered over is concealed from view, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Does something innovative, suggesting bankers?

blocks.note: surface reading: hinting at people who work in banks
setter's reading: in crosswords a banker is a river, and a river that bursts its banks cuts a fresh course across the land

explanation.surface: Someone pioneering a new idea, perhaps in the world of finance.
explanation.walkthrough: A river shifting its course literally breaks into land it never crossed before, the idea the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing pioneering work nobody has attempted before, which is acting innovatively.

clue.text: Western city has no lasagne unfortunately

indicators.note: things that turn out unfortunately go awry, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant review grumbling that a town out West has no Italian food on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' looks like it removes the pasta dish, but its two letters join the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: This city lies in western Texas, and 'Western' suggests the American West of cowboy films.

clue.text: Nastier king leaving more frozen

indicators.note: when something is leaving it departs, so a letter drops out

blocks.note: ickier means more unpleasant
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Things got worse when the king departed, and the weather turned colder too.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier is the comparative of icy, describing something colder and more covered with ice.

clue.text: Genuine, busy young woman lacking experience

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing a sincere, hard-working newcomer who is still green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genuine' reads as an adjective for the young woman, but it supplies all the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is an innocent, unsophisticated girl, especially the stock role of one on stage.

clue.text: Female saint (queen) rejected each clever scheme

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so that letter is removed from the saint's name

blocks.note: Saint Brigid is one of Ireland's patron saints
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
ea. is the standard abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: A queen turned down every plan a woman saint put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A big idea is an ambitious or ingenious plan, often said ironically, so it fits a scheme thought clever.

clue.text: Company mate’s one of 2

indicators.note: the answer to 2 down names letter rearrangements, so this is a rearranged version of the word before

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend belongs to one of two firms.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the entry at 2 down, which names the very rearrangement needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a group of people working together, one sense of a company, as in a theatre company.

clue.text: Ancestors’ DNA sets can get misconstrued

indicators.note: misconstrued means wrongly put together, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that genetic tests tracing family history can be misread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendants are forebears, people from whom one is descended, the opposite of descendants.

clue.text: Rock star Jeremy’s air

blocks.note: Jeremy Irons is an Oscar-winning English actor
an air is a tune, and tone is its musical quality

explanation.surface: A rock star called Jeremy and his public persona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock star' reads as one phrase about music, but 'Rock' alone is the definition and the star is an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone is a sedimentary rock rich in iron ore.

clue.text: End of breathing tube is torn and left at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A diver's snorkel has ripped and been abandoned in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Each nostril is an external opening of the nose, where the airway through which we breathe ends.

clue.text: A riddle, sweetened tea perhaps is one

blocks.note: char is British slang for tea
an ade is a sweetened fruit drink, as in lemonade

explanation.surface: Someone puzzling over whether a sugary cup of tea counts as a riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetened tea' read as tea plus a sweet drink is built exactly like a clue of this very kind, which is what 'perhaps is one' points out.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a riddle or word game where a word is acted out or pieced together syllable by syllable.

clue.text: Best desserts not cold for once, tasty at the beginning

indicators.note: not means without, so one letter is left out
at the beginning points to the very first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: choc ices are ice-cream bars coated in chocolate, a British favourite
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the first letter of tasty

explanation.surface: For a change, the finest puddings are served warm, with the tasty ones first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for once' reminds you that only one of the two C's goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Choicest is the superlative of choice in its adjective sense of excellent, so it means the finest.

clue.text: This starts from any crossword, reading of sign that is clear

definitions.text: This starts from any crossword, reading of sign that is clear

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are taken, one from each

blocks.clueFragment: any crossword, reading of sign that is clear
blocks.note: the opening letters of the eight words

explanation.surface: Advice that a puzzle becomes plain once you read the signs properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is itself an example of the answer: its word initials spell it out.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a text in which the first letters of each line or word spell something, exactly what the clue does.

clue.text: This might be 5 or 24 interpretation

blocks.note: first meaning: with the answers at 5 and 24, the kinds of clue that are double or cryptic ones of this word
second meaning: an explanation of what something means

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references give DOUBLE and CRYPTIC, two clue types whose names end in this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition states or interprets the meaning of a word, and double and cryptic versions are both standard clue types.

clue.text: Theatre workers are 23 guys

guys are men

explanation.surface: Backstage crew described as smart fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Flymen work above the stage in the fly loft, raising and lowering scenery on ropes.

clue.text: Method of army signals after cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from the front to the back, as on a wheel

blocks.note: tic-tac is the hand-signalling code used by British racecourse bookmakers

explanation.surface: Military communications sent after a bicycle ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army signals' looks like one phrase, but 'army' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre, and military tactics are the methods an army uses in battle.

clue.text: Out of uniform, retired conductor is a bore

indicators.note: out of means without, so that letter goes missing
something retired has withdrawn backwards, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Uniform is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for U
a train guard is the British name for a conductor

explanation.surface: An off-duty conductor, now in civvies, turns out to be tedious company.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag is informally something or someone tiresome and dull, the same sense as a bore.

clue.text: Wilful cruelty depicted by pictures is trendy

blocks.note: S and M stands for sadism and masochism
pictures are works of art

explanation.surface: Fashionable modern paintings that portray deliberate cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart can mean stylish and fashionable, as in the smart set, so it matches trendy.

clue.text: Strange vault I see

I stays, and see is said like the letter C

explanation.surface: Someone peering into a strange burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means mysterious or obscure in meaning, so it serves as a synonym for strange or puzzling.

clue.text: Recovers from company sad musical

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
mesto is the Italian musical direction to play sadly

explanation.surface: A theatre group bouncing back after staging a depressing show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical' reads as a noun for a show, but it marks the word that follows as a score marking.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to regain consciousness, so someone who comes to is recovering after fainting.

clue.text: Lots of water buffalo ultimately stir, eating the middle of reeds

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter is kept
eating takes something inside, so one piece goes into the other
the central letter of the next word is the only one wanted

blocks.note: the final letter of buffalo
stir and can are both slang for prison
the central letter of reeds

explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast expanse of sea water, so it is a huge quantity of water.

clue.text: Entry by passage right for college

indicators.note: one thing for another means it stands in that place instead

blocks.note: by and in are interchangeable in phrases such as by or in the evening
a passage of text is a section of it
R is the abbreviation for right
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: Getting into a university by switching from one college to another and finding the right way in.
explanation.definitionFit: An insertion is something put in, such as an entry added to a text or register.
